title: Protocol for quantifying the germination properties of individual bacterial endospores using PySpore
protocol: Clean coverslip (#1.5H thickness) using 70% ethanol followed by deionized water.
Wipe the cleaned coverslip with a folded Kimwipe without crumpling it to avoid excessive lint.
Draw a 3 × 2 grid on a coverslip using permanent marker.
Spot 2–3 μL diluted spores onto their respective grid position and let the spots dry for 20–30 min at 37°C or 30–60 min at ∼25°C.
Clean two standard microscope slides with 70% ethanol followed by deionized water.
Remove solid adhesive backing from a Gene Frame, leaving one side adhered, and adhere to the center of one clean slide.
Prepare a 3.5% solution of low melting point agarose in deionized water.
Make a 2× concentrated solution of media/buffer for germination containing germinant signals.
Vortex 1 mL molten agarose and 1 mL 2× media thoroughly.
Quickly pipette 500 μL of the mixed solution into the well created by the Gene Frame.
Cover with another clean microscope slide quickly.
Press the top slide down firmly on the Gene Frame.
Let solidify at 4°C for 30 min.
Let solidify at 25°C for 2–5 h.
Ensure that the agarose pad equilibrates to the temperature of the experiment (e.g., 25°C or 37°C).
Add a coverslip once the agarose pad has reached the appropriate temperature.
Set up image acquisition parameters.
Select a 60–100× high numerical aperture phase-contrast oil immersion objective.
Find a suitable illumination intensity and exposure time to avoid saturated pixels.
Set the experiment duration optimized for your experiment.
Set a sampling interval of 30 seconds maximum to avoid under-sampling.
Inoculate spores onto an agarose pad.
Remove the top slide from the agarose pad.
Pull off the top adhesive backing and let the pad dry for 3–5 minutes at 25°C.
Carefully place the coverslip with adhered spores on the agar pad, sealing the edges.
Place the slide on the stage insert, ensuring it accommodates a standard glass slide.
Immediately pick two different XY positions throughout each sample.
Begin imaging within 1-1.5 minutes after placing the sample.
Ensure multiple XY positions are chosen to allow for useful data acquisition even if one goes out of focus.
Add a "wait" command of 100–500 milliseconds to ensure oil is spread evenly on the top lens.
Choose positions that are not too crowded and avoid clumps to maintain accurate segmentation.
Preprocess images.
Crop out-of-focus regions from the images.
Export files in tagged image format (.tif).
Trim the number of frames as needed.
Ensure filenames contain the channel and position information.
Launch PySpore.
Click on the “Launch Image Processing” button within the launcher.
Select "Browse" from the top of the GUI.
Navigate to the directory containing the pre-processed images.
Load an image by selecting it and clicking the “Load Image” icon.
Adjust the threshold value for optimal segmentation, typically ranging between 0.05-0.15.
Click “Test Segmentation” to display an image showing spore outlines generated.
Use the frame slider at the bottom of the window to view all images in the stack.
Optimize thresholds by testing multiple time points in the movie.
